Definition: Top-down amplification of error units, leading to disinhibited gain in response to attended or highly precise stimuli.
Tag: Qualitative, Contexts: LO+GO.
Our study text: It mentions that "prediction-error signals are specific to the features of the unexpected visual input" and that they are amplified in highly selective neurons. This is consistent with a precision weighting mechanism where only stimulus-selective neurons show amplification. So factor 10 is supported moderately; I assign maybe +0.6 because it's qualitative evidence but clearly observed.

Factor 11: E/I Balance Shift
Definition: Dynamic adjustment toward higher inhibition for predictable stimuli, leading to suppressed neural firing.
Tag: Quantitative, Contexts: LO+GO.
Our study text: They show that expected stimuli do not lead to increased responses (or they remain constant) while unexpected ones are amplified. This could be interpreted as a shift in E/I balance: For expected inputs, there is maintained inhibition leading to suppression of firing; for prediction error, disinhibition occurs. So factor 11 seems supported moderately quantitatively. I assign +0.6.

Factor 12: Omission Response
Definition: A top-down generated internal signal in the absence of prediction-mediated suppression, revealing the raw expectation.
Tag: Quantitative, Contexts: LO+GO.
Our study text: They mention that "some neurons responded to omission of an expected stimulus" (Extended Data Fig. 2e,f). So there is evidence for omission responses. The effect was significant (P < 1×10^-4) for omission response signals. This is quantitative and supports the factor. I assign +0.6 maybe.

Now Group H2: Feedforward Error Propagation:

Factor 13: Feedforward Deviance Detection
Definition: Detection of mismatch signals that explicitly propagate in the feedforward (ascending) direction to higher cortical areas.
Tag: Quantitative, Contexts: LO+GO.
Our study text: It discusses "prediction-error signal" and how it is transmitted via V1 responses. But does it mention feedforward deviance detection? The study focuses on V1 layer 2/3 neurons in response to unexpected stimuli. However, the propagation of prediction errors to higher areas is not explicitly measured here; they are recording local V1 responses only, not their projection to higher areas. They do record from V1 and then mention pulvinar inputs which come from thalamus (which could be feedforward). But direct evidence for "feedforward deviance detection" is not provided in this study because it focuses on V1 responses rather than ascending propagation. So factor 13: I assign null.

Factor 14: Feedforward AMPA
Definition: Fast excitatory drive mediated by AMPA receptors, specifically conveying prediction-error signals in the feedforward direction.
Tag: Quantitative, Contexts: LO+GO.
Our study text: It does not mention AMPA receptor kinetics. They use calcium imaging and mention timing of responses but don't measure AMPA receptor-specific contributions. So factor 14 gets null.

Factor 15: Feedforward NMDA
Definition: Voltage-dependent amplification (bursting) of error signals, facilitating their robust feedforward propagation through the hierarchy.
Tag: Quantitative, Contexts: LO+GO.
Our study text: Not mentioned. Null.

Factor 16: Feedforward Ascending Gamma
Definition: Rhythmic synchronization (30-90Hz) that temporally packages prediction-error signals for efficient feedforward transmission.
Tag: Quantitative, Contexts: LO+GO.
Not addressed; null.

Factor 17: Absence of Feedback Error
Definition: The functional requirement that the prediction-error signal must be strictly feedforward-directed, distinguishing it from local or feedback signals.
Tag: Quantitative, Contexts: LO+GO.
Our study text: They show that unexpected stimuli produce amplified responses in V1 and also mention that "neural responses were not correlated with running speed" etc. But they do not explicitly test whether the signal is feedforward as opposed to feedback. There's a discussion about pulvinar input which is thalamic (feedforward from higher areas) though it might be considered feedforward? However, the text does mention "pulvinar projections" and then later optogenetic inactivation of pulvinar axons reduces unexpected responses. That suggests that part of the prediction error signal depends on feedforward input from the thalamus (subcortical relay). And they also show that VIP neurons are recruited by both novel and familiar stimuli at unexpected locations. The study does not directly address whether there's absence of feedback error signals. It might be inferred indirectly because they inactivate pulvinar inputs and see reduction in response, which supports the idea that feedforward (pulvinar) input is necessary. But then they also mention that V1 responses are abolished when VIP neurons are silenced, suggesting that the signal is not solely due to local feedback but requires feedforward input. However, "Absence of Feedback Error" specifically means that prediction error signals do not contain feedback components. The study does not measure or comment on feedback errors directly. So factor 17: I assign null.

Factor 18: Feedforward Non-local Supragranular Activity (L2/3)
Definition: Error-signaling neurons in Layers 2/3 projecting strictly into the next area, and NOT projecting inside the column serving as the primary anatomical source for feedforward signal propagation.
Tag: Quantitative, Contexts: LO+GO.
The study text: They record from layer 2/3 neurons in V1. And they discuss that prediction-error signals are observed in L2/3. However, do they show that these cells project to the next area? They don't measure projection patterns. They mention "feedforward non-local" but then later they talk about pulvinar input and VIP neurons. There's no direct evidence for feedforward connectivity from V1 L2/3 to other areas. So factor 18: null.
